sara_support: Escalation from Tier 1 - customer reports SSE streams abruptly cut mid-event when routed through Cloudflare + NLB to our private runtime. They see truncated `data:` lines and the client auto-reconnects in a tight loop. Ticket INC-3821 attached.

mike_sre: Do we have a sample of the truncated payload or a packet capture? Which clients are impacted (browser, mobile, corporate proxy)?

sara_support: They supplied a small capture and timeline. Browser = Chrome desktop + Android WebView. Snippet from their capture (IDs redacted):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"id":"evt-77","text":"Partial start of a long message that ends abruptly here"
# socket closed by origin / client reconnect
```

sara_support: Customer says on reconnect sometimes they receive the remainder of the event, sometimes a duplicate, sometimes nothing. It seems correlated with streams being idle for > ~70s.

olivia_eng: This smells like proxy/load-balancer idle behavior + buffering interaction. If Cloudflare or a worker is buffering/compressing, chunk boundaries can be altered. Also check ALB vs NLB: ALB (HTTP) may tear down connections differently than NLB (TCP).

mike_sre: I reproduced locally on staging: simple SSE app behind Cloudflare -> NLB -> runtime. `curl -v -N --http1.1 https://staging.example/stream` with server sending an event, idle 90s, then close. Observed origin side FIN while the proxy had partially forwarded a chunk. TCP trace shows origin FIN immediately after sending a fragment. Browser behavior varied across reconnects.

jamie_prod: Repro steps to ask customer (keep short):
1) `curl -v -N --http1.1 https://$HOST/v1/stream` (note `-N` disables curls stdout buffering)
2) Server: emit a large SSE event (>2KB), sleep 90s, then close connection
3) Share full curl verbose output including headers and reconnect output

olivia_eng: From runtime side we should recommend these best-practices to customers: flush each SSE event, do not set Content-Length, ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, disable response compression for SSE endpoints (or set `Content-Encoding: identity`), and send periodic comments/pings to avoid idle closes. Also consider `X-Accel-Buffering: no`-style headers for proxies where supported.

mike_sre: Short-term mitigations we can suggest immediately:
- Disable gzip on SSE endpoints (fastest fix)
- Configure Cloudflare route to bypass response buffering (Page Rule or Worker)
- Increase idle timeouts on LB (ALB idle default 60s; NLB TCP idle up to 350s configurable)
- Add a heartbeat comment `:hb\n\n` every 15s from the server to keep the connection active

jamie_prod: I added a small Node repro client that reconnects and prints raw chunks:
```
const https = require('https');\nfunction connect(){\n  https.get('https://staging.example/stream', {headers:{'Connection':'keep-alive'}}, res=>{\n    res.on('data', d=>process.stdout.write(d));\n    res.on('end', ()=>{ setTimeout(connect,200); });\n  });\n}\nconnect();\n```

olivia_eng: From our runtime team: we'll add an internal header that reduces downstream buffering for `text/event-stream` and document SSE setup behind CF/NLB. File an ENG ticket for the header + docs.

mike_sre: Collected some proxy logs from staging run (sanitized):
```
[proxy] accept conn from CF 10.0.0.12 -> origin 10.0.2.45
[proxy] forward resp: 200 chunked
[proxy] write chunk "data: {..partial..}\n"
[proxy] origin FIN received
[proxy] client socket closed after partial write
```

mike_sre: When origin FINs mid-chunk, proxies may not finish chunk metadata or may flush an incomplete chunk, leaving browsers with a half event. On reconnect some clients try to reassemble and dedupe which explains inconsistent outcomes.

sara_support: Action items for support to request from the customer:
- Run the `curl -v -N` test above and paste the full output
- Temporarily disable gzip for the SSE route and retry
- If on Cloudflare, try a page rule to disable response buffering for the SSE path or set the route to "Bypass"
- Provide client UA and whether there are corporate/network proxies in front of the client

mike_sre: I'll prepare a small tracer that logs chunk boundaries and TCP FIN/RST timing on staging to precisely map where the fragmentation occurs.

olivia_eng: I'll open ENGRTC-142 to track: runtime header for no-buffering, docs for SSE behind CF/NLB, and an internal runbook for support.

sara_support: Thanks team. I'll add these instructions to INC-3821 and ask the customer to try toggling gzip. Will report back when they respond. :thumbsup:
